adjudication.evidence: Original N/E/U show two distinct step-like offsets: one at ~577 (down in N, up in E/U) and another at ~631 (up in N/E/U). P3 (577–631) spans the interval between them but lacks a sustained return; interior observations (578–630) show no recovery toward pre-577 levels—instead, they remain offset, indicating a permanent step at 577, not a temporary platform. P4 and P5 are single-day spikes coinciding with the second step onset; their opposite-signed offsets suggest they represent the return edge of a *different* temporary event, but the original U/E/N do not show a sustained post-631 return to pre-631 levels—rather, they settle at a new level, implying a permanent step at 631. No pair shows both a sustained shift and opposing return across the same axes. Thus, no genuine temporary platform exists in this interval.
